fundamental.name: fundamental
fundamental.method: drum_verify.spectrum (Hann over the first 0.500 s, 262144-point rfft) -> parabolic-interpolated maximum inside 20-2000 Hz
fundamental.channel: mono: the drum buses summed through drums_fx.output_fx
fundamental.resample_hz: none: rendered and analysed at 48000 Hz
fundamental.filter: the maximum is restricted to drum_verify.BAND['BD'] = 20-2000 Hz; the signal itself is not filtered
fundamental.normalisation: none: a frequency, unaffected by level

fft.transform: real FFT of a Hann-windowed segment
fft.hop: one transform of one segment, not a spectrogram

fit_quality.model: parabolic interpolation of the three bins around the maximum
fit_quality.uncertainty_basis: half the 0.1831 Hz bin spacing before interpolation improves it
fit_quality.noise_floor_treatment: the maximum is taken inside the band, so the -103.0 dB mean level above it cannot become the peak

selection.interval_basis: from the trimmed onset, capped at 0.5 s so a long tail does not dilute the transform (drum_verify.measure's own rule)

decay tau.name: decay tau
decay tau.method: drum_verify.trim_onset -> moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) -> drum_verify.decay_fit, least squares on the log-envelope between -3 and -30 dB of its peak
decay tau.channel: mono: the drum buses summed through drums_fx.output_fx
decay tau.resample_hz: none: rendered and analysed at 48000 Hz
decay tau.filter: none on the envelope path -- the envelope is a moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) of the full-band signal; drum_verify.BAND is applied to the spectrum rows only
decay tau.normalisation: none (absolute full scale); the decay is measured relative to the envelope's own peak, so a gain change cannot move it

fft.window: moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental)
fft.hop: none: the envelope is evaluated at every sample

fit_quality.model: least squares on the log-envelope, dB vs s
fit_quality.uncertainty_basis: 1 sigma on tau, propagated from the least-squares covariance of the log-envelope slope
fit_quality.noise_floor_treatment: the fit stops at the first sample -30.0 dB below the envelope peak; the render's last 50 ms sits at -41.8 dB, so no sample inside the floor enters the fit

T20.name: T20
T20.method: drum_verify.trim_onset -> moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) -> the first sample at or below -20 dB of the envelope peak, in ms from the peak. A threshold crossing, not a fit
T20.channel: mono: the drum buses summed through drums_fx.output_fx
T20.resample_hz: none: rendered and analysed at 48000 Hz
T20.filter: none on the envelope path -- the envelope is a moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) of the full-band signal; drum_verify.BAND is applied to the spectrum rows only
T20.normalisation: none (absolute full scale); the decay is measured relative to the envelope's own peak, so a gain change cannot move it

fft.window: moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental)
fft.hop: none: the envelope is evaluated at every sample

fit_quality.model: none: a crossing is located, not fitted
fit_quality.uncertainty_basis: +/-1 sample (0.0208 ms); the envelope's own smoothing window is the larger term and is stated in fft.window
fit_quality.noise_floor_treatment: -20 dB is far above this render's floor, so the crossing is on signal; a floor above -20 dB would make this metric meaningless and is recorded for that check

attack.name: attack
attack.method: drum_verify.trim_onset -> moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) -> drum_verify.attack_ms: the 2 %-of-peak crossing of the envelope to the envelope's peak
attack.channel: mono: the drum buses summed through drums_fx.output_fx
attack.resample_hz: none: rendered and analysed at 48000 Hz
attack.filter: none on the envelope path -- the envelope is a moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental) of the full-band signal; drum_verify.BAND is applied to the spectrum rows only
attack.normalisation: none (absolute full scale); the decay is measured relative to the envelope's own peak, so a gain change cannot move it

fft.window: moving RMS, drum_verify.ENV_WIN_MS[voice] ms (several periods of the voice's own fundamental)
fft.hop: none: the envelope is evaluated at every sample

fit_quality.uncertainty_basis: +/-1 sample (0.0208 ms) on each end; the envelope window is what sets the real resolution, and is why this metric moves when the envelope method changes
fit_quality.noise_floor_treatment: the 2 % threshold is 34 dB below the peak; the measured floor is the check that it is above it
